note: DRAFT v1 module checks and final knowledge check for CARSI Building Science Foundations. Original CARSI questions for Australian and New Zealand conditions; no IICRC standard text reproduced. Every option in a question has the same word count. The final quiz id is kept from the live seed with new questions. SME review required before seeding.

quizzes.title: CARSI Building Science Foundations — Module 1 check

questions.questionText: A closed room warms from 22 °C to 28 °C and nothing is dried. Which number stays the same?
options: Relative humidity as percentage
Humidity ratio in g/kg
Dry-bulb temperature in °C
Saturation vapour pressure, hPa
questions.explanation: Humidity ratio changes only when water is added or removed. RH falls as the air warms, and saturation vapour pressure rises with temperature.

questions.questionText: A log shows RH falling from 80 % to 56 % while the room warmed. What does that prove on its own?
options: Water has left the air
The dehumidifier is working well
Nothing about water removal yet
The materials are now dry
questions.explanation: RH depends on temperature. Warming alone lowers RH, so you need g/kg or dew point to show that water has actually left the air.

questions.questionText: What is the dew point of an air sample?
options: The temperature where dew begins forming
The highest temperature the room reaches
The surface temperature of wet timber
The mean RH reading each morning
questions.explanation: The Bureau of Meteorology defines dew point as the temperature to which air must be cooled, at constant pressure, for dew to occur.

questions.questionText: Air is 25 °C and 60 %RH at 1013.25 hPa. What is its humidity ratio?
options: About 8.7 g/kg
About 11.9 g/kg
About 14.9 g/kg
About 19.0 g/kg

questions.questionText: An imported spec sheet quotes 70 grains per pound. What is that in g/kg?
options: About 7 g/kg
About 10 g/kg
About 49 g/kg
About 490 g/kg
questions.explanation: From the NIST grain and pound factors, 1 g/kg is 7.0 grains per pound, so 70 ÷ 7.0 = 10 g/kg.

questions.questionText: Why should you be able to calculate dew point by hand?
options: To check an instrument for errors
Because meters never display dew point
Because insurers ban all electronic meters
To avoid recording any RH readings
questions.explanation: Instruments can be set to the wrong unit, fog up or read before settling. Working the numbers yourself shows when a screen is wrong.

quizzes.title: CARSI Building Science Foundations — Module 2 check

questions.questionText: What drives water to evaporate from a wet surface?
options: The noise level of the air movers
Surface vapour pressure above air vapour pressure
The exact colour of the wet material
The total number of dehumidifiers on site
questions.explanation: Evaporation runs on the gap between the surface vapour pressure, about es at the surface temperature, and the vapour pressure of the air.

questions.questionText: A wet wall is at 20 °C (es 23.39 hPa) and the room air has e = 16.37 hPa. What is Δp?
options: About 7.0 hPa
About 16.4 hPa
About 23.4 hPa
About 39.8 hPa
questions.explanation: Δp = es(surface) − e(air) = 23.39 − 16.37 = 7.02 hPa.

questions.questionText: What does airflow across a wet surface actually do?
options: It creates a new driving force
It lets the existing difference act
It raises the surface vapour pressure
It removes water from the building
questions.explanation: Airflow replaces the near-saturated layer at the surface with room air so the existing Δp can act. It does not create a driving force or remove vapour from the building.

questions.questionText: A floor surface is 8 °C in a Canberra room at 10 °C and 85 %RH. Which lever helps most?
options: Adding air movers to the laundry
Opening the front and back doors
Warming the wet floor surface up
Covering the floor with plastic sheeting
questions.explanation: A cold surface has a low es, so Δp starts near 0.3 hPa. Warming the floor to 18 °C lifts Δp to about 10.2 hPa, far more than drying the air alone.

questions.questionText: Why is heat used together with vapour removal, never instead of it?
options: Heat alone lets room g/kg climb
Heat always damages timber flooring boards
Heat stops all evaporation from surfaces
Heat lowers the room dew point
questions.explanation: Warming lowers RH but not g/kg. As materials release water the room g/kg rises, and that warm moist air can condense on cooler surfaces.

questions.questionText: You see suspected mould growth on a wet wall. What happens before air movers run?
options: Run them on high straight away
Stop and plan under mould training
Spray the wall with plain water
Point every unit at the growth
questions.explanation: Moving air across visible or suspected growth is a separate decision. Stop and plan the job under CARSI mould remediation training first.

quizzes.title: CARSI Building Science Foundations — Module 3 check

questions.questionText: A sample weighs 58.4 g wet and 50.0 g oven-dry. What is its moisture content?
options: About 8.4 %
About 14.4 %
About 16.8 %
About 58.4 %
questions.explanation: MC = (wet − dry) ÷ dry × 100 = (58.4 − 50.0) ÷ 50.0 × 100 = 16.8 %, on an oven-dry basis.

questions.questionText: A meter shows 18 WME on plasterboard. What does that reading mean?
options: The board holds 18 % water
Reads as wood at 18 %
The board is completely dry now
The board needs replacing at once
questions.explanation: WME is the reading the material would give if it were wood. It is a comparison scale, used against an unaffected reading of the same material.

questions.questionText: Two meters disagree on one joist. What should you check first?
options: The species and scale settings used
The brand of each meter case
The colour of the timber surface
The time the insurer was called
questions.explanation: Pin meters convert resistance to moisture content with a wood calibration, so species and scale settings change the number shown.

questions.questionText: What is equilibrium moisture content (EMC)?
options: The moisture content after oven drying
The highest moisture content timber reaches
Where wood neither gains nor loses
The reading on a pinless meter
questions.explanation: The Wood Handbook defines EMC as the moisture content at which wood is neither gaining nor losing moisture, set by the air temperature and RH.

questions.questionText: Where should the drying goal for a timber floor come from?
options: A universal 12 % for every job
The builder’s preferred number on the day
Unaffected same material, same meter and setting
The wettest reading taken on day one
questions.explanation: Readings on the same material in unaffected areas, with the same meter and setting, reflect this building, climate and season. No single number does.

questions.questionText: A wall reads damp on a meter. What can you report from that alone?
options: Mould is growing inside the wall
Occupants have been exposed to mould
The material is damp right there
The wall must be demolished today
questions.explanation: A moisture reading is a moisture finding. It shows conditions that could support growth, not that growth is present or that anyone was exposed.

quizzes.title: CARSI Building Science Foundations — Module 4 check

questions.questionText: Room 18 °C, outside −0.1 °C, window U 6.2, Rsi 0.13. About how cold is the inside glass?
options: About 3.4 °C
About 10.7 °C
About 14.6 °C
About 18.0 °C

questions.questionText: What does a lower window U-value mean?
options: More heat flows through the window
Better resistance to heat flowing through
The glass lets in less daylight
The frame is made of aluminium
questions.explanation: YourHome explains that the lower the U-value, the greater the window’s resistance to heat flow, so its inside surface stays warmer.

questions.questionText: Where do thermal bridges commonly make inside surfaces colder?
options: Corners, framing and around window openings
Ceiling fans and light fittings only
Carpet laid over a timber floor
The middle of an insulated wall
questions.explanation: The ABCB handbook names corners of walls and window and door openings as vulnerable, along with insulation interrupted by framing.

questions.questionText: Room air has a dew point of 11.3 °C. A window surface reads 10.7 °C. What follows?
options: Condensation cannot form on it
Condensation can form on it
There must be a leak
It sits above dew point
questions.explanation: The surface is 0.6 °C below the room dew point, so condensation can form there.

questions.questionText: In an air-conditioned Brisbane house in summer, where is condensation most likely?
options: On the outside of the windows
Inside the wall behind the lining
On the carpet in the hallway
On the ceiling of the garage
questions.explanation: Cooling makes the lining the cold side. Humid outside air in the wall can meet that cold surface, as YourHome and the ABCB handbook describe.

questions.questionText: Which pattern points to condensation rather than a leak?
options: It appears only after the shower
It follows cold nights and settings
It spreads from one pipe joint
It is worse after heavy rain
questions.explanation: Condensation follows the weather and the thermostat and collects on the coldest surfaces. A leak follows pipework or rain and spreads from a point.

quizzes.title: CARSI Building Science Foundations — Module 5 check

questions.questionText: A 33.6 m³ bathroom has a 50 L/s fan. What is its rated air change rate?
options: About 1.5 ACH
About 2.1 ACH
About 5.4 ACH
About 15.0 ACH

questions.questionText: CO2 falls from 1800 to 900 ppm in 0.5 h, outdoors 420 ppm. What is the ACH?
options: About 0.7 ACH
About 1.4 ACH
About 2.1 ACH
About 4.2 ACH

questions.questionText: Why must the room be empty during a CO2 decay test?
options: People breathe out extra CO2 gas
People block the exhaust fan grille
The insurer requires an empty room
CO2 sensors cannot read near people
questions.explanation: People emit CO2, so they would add tracer during the decay. The ventilation review by McNeill and others says the room must be unoccupied.

questions.questionText: Inside is 14.9 g/kg and outside is 14.2 g/kg. Should you ventilate to dry?
options: Yes, ventilation will dry it fast
No, it barely removes any water
Yes, because outside RH is lower
No, because ventilation always adds water
questions.explanation: The difference is under 1 g/kg, so swapping air removes very little and lets humid air past the dehumidifiers.

questions.questionText: Why compare g/kg rather than RH when deciding to ventilate?
options: RH depends on each air’s temperature
g/kg is easier to read aloud
RH is only measured at airports
g/kg ignores the outdoor conditions entirely
questions.explanation: RH depends on temperature, so a cold outdoor air with high RH can still carry less water than warm indoor air.

questions.questionText: What balance does NZ Building Code clause E3 ask for in wet spaces?
options: Thermal resistance, ventilation and space temperature
Paint colour, flooring type and lighting
Window size, door width, roof pitch
Plumbing pressure, pipe size and taps
questions.explanation: Clause E3.3.1 asks for an adequate combination of thermal resistance, ventilation and space temperature where moisture may be generated or accumulate.

questions.questionText: Which NCC climate zone includes Brisbane?
options: Climate zone 1
Climate zone 2
Climate zone 5
Climate zone 7
questions.explanation: The ABCB lists Brisbane, Coffs Harbour and Mackay as typical climate zone 2 locations.

questions.questionText: What are NCC climatic zones A, B and C used for?
options: Energy-efficiency insulation R-values for walls
Subfloor ventilation from seasonal RH
Bushfire attack level rating categories
Cyclonic wind loads on roofs
questions.explanation: Zones A, B and C are a separate classification based on seasonal RH, used for subfloor ventilation. They are not the eight climate zones.

questions.questionText: A NZ rental has a suspended floor over an enclosed subfloor. What do Healthy Homes rules require?
options: A ground moisture barrier
A concrete slab instead
Mechanical subfloor heating fitted
A subfloor dehumidifier unit
questions.explanation: The Healthy Homes Standards require an enclosed subfloor under a suspended floor to have a ground moisture barrier.

quizzes.title: CARSI Building Science Foundations — Module 6 check

questions.questionText: July mean minimum is −0.1 °C and the estimated dew point is 1.6 °C. What follows?
options: Outdoor overnight condensation is quite likely
Outdoor condensation is impossible that month
There is definitely a roof leak
Indoor RH will be zero overnight
questions.explanation: Where the mean minimum falls below the dew point, the ABCB handbook says condensation may occur, so dew or frost outside is expected.

questions.questionText: Where do New Zealand jobs get long-term station climate data?
options: NIWA’s National Climate Database via DataHub
The Australian Bureau of Meteorology tables
The dehumidifier maker’s printed product brochure
An insurer’s online claim lodgement form
questions.explanation: NIWA provides access to New Zealand’s National Climate Database through its DataHub service.

questions.questionText: Why treat a dew point from mean 9 am figures as approximate?
options: The Bureau calls its RH means approximations
Dew point cannot be calculated at all
Temperatures are only recorded in the summer
The station never records any relative humidity
questions.explanation: The Bureau notes its RH statistics do not fully account for the temperature dependence of RH and are approximations only.

questions.questionText: Inlet air is 11.19 g/kg and outlet air is 6.49 g/kg. What is the grain depression?
options: About 4.70 g/kg
About 6.49 g/kg
About 11.19 g/kg
About 17.68 g/kg
questions.explanation: Depression = inlet humidity ratio − outlet humidity ratio = 11.19 − 6.49 = 4.70 g/kg.

questions.questionText: Airflow 400 m³/h, density 1.19 kg/m³, depression 4.70 g/kg. About how much water per hour?
options: About 0.2 L/h
About 2.2 L/h
About 5.6 L/h
About 22 L/h
questions.explanation: 400 × 1.19 × 4.70 ÷ 1000 = 2.24 kg, about 2.2 L of water per hour.

questions.questionText: The room is still wet but a dehumidifier’s depression has collapsed. What next?
options: Check its filter, coil and airflow
Declare the room dry and leave
Open every window in the house
Turn off all the air movers
questions.explanation: Depression should shrink slowly as a room dries. A collapse while the room is still wet points to the unit, so check it before trusting its numbers.

quizzes.title: CARSI Building Science Foundations — Final Knowledge Check

questions.questionText: Air warms from 18 °C to 26 °C with no water added or removed. What happens?
options: RH rises, g/kg stays the same
RH falls, g/kg stays the same
RH falls, g/kg falls as well
RH stays, g/kg rises a little
questions.explanation: Warming lowers RH because the air could hold more vapour, but the grams of water per kilogram of dry air do not change.

questions.questionText: What is the dew point of air at 25 °C and 60 %RH?
options: About 12.0 °C
About 19.0 °C
About 21.3 °C
About 16.7 °C

questions.questionText: Which formula gives humidity ratio in g/kg from vapour pressure e and pressure P?
questions.explanation: The NWS mixing ratio formula is w = 621.97 × e ÷ (P − e), with e and P in the same pressure units.

questions.questionText: Room air at 20 °C has e = 10.53 hPa and the wet wall is 20 °C. What is Δp?
options: About 7.0 hPa
About 10.5 hPa
About 12.9 hPa
About 23.4 hPa

questions.questionText: In a cold Canberra laundry, which lever usually moves Δp the most?
options: Warming the wet material up
Adding more air movers alone
Opening the laundry door wide
Lowering the room temperature further
questions.explanation: A cold surface has a low es. Warming it raises es steeply, which lifts the driving force far more than airflow or small changes in room air.

questions.questionText: Why does a wet wall often read cooler than the room?
options: Evaporation cools the surface it leaves
Plasterboard is always colder than air
Moisture meters cool the wall down
Air movers blow cold outside air
questions.explanation: Evaporation takes heat from the surface, the same effect the Bureau describes in a wet-bulb thermometer.

questions.questionText: On what basis is timber moisture content calculated?
options: Mass of water over wet mass
Mass of water over oven-dry mass
Volume of water over board volume
Meter reading over the room RH
questions.explanation: The Wood Handbook defines MC as the mass of water divided by the oven-dry mass of the wood, so MC can exceed 100 %.

questions.questionText: Wood at 21.1 °C and 45 %RH settles near which EMC in the Wood Handbook table?
options: About 6.2 %
About 8.5 %
About 12.0 %
About 16.0 %
questions.explanation: Table 4-2 of the Wood Handbook gives about 8.5 % at 21.1 °C and 45 %RH.

questions.questionText: A builder says every floor must reach 12 %. What is the best reply?
options: Agree, because 12 % suits every house
Set the goal from unaffected material here
Dry it to zero per cent instead
Use the wettest reading as the target
questions.explanation: EMC varies with the room and season, so the dry standard comes from unaffected same material with the same meter and setting on this job.

questions.questionText: A damp reading on a wall lining proves which of these?
options: Mould is definitely growing there
An occupant has been exposed
The lining is damp there
The lining must come out
questions.explanation: A meter reading is a moisture finding only. Growth and exposure need separate assessment.

questions.questionText: Room 18 °C, outside −0.1 °C, window U 3.1, Rsi 0.13. About how cold is the inside glass?
options: About 3.4 °C
About 7.3 °C
About 10.7 °C
About 14.6 °C

questions.questionText: What is the surface condensation check?
options: Compare surface temperature with warm-side dew point
Compare the outdoor RH with indoor RH
Compare meter readings on two different materials
Compare the fan label with room volume
questions.explanation: If a surface is at or below the dew point of the air on its warm side, condensation can form there.

questions.questionText: For NCC climate zone 1, where does the ABCB say cooled buildings often condense?
options: The layer just behind the interior lining
The outside face of the roof sheeting
The top surface of the concrete driveway
The glass of every single external window
questions.explanation: The ABCB handbook says that in climate zone 1 the layer immediately behind the interior lining is often the coldest surface at risk when spaces are cooled.

questions.questionText: Label airflow is 180 m³/h in a 33.6 m³ room. What is the rated ACH?
options: About 0.2 ACH
About 2.1 ACH
About 5.4 ACH
About 6.0 ACH
questions.explanation: ACH = airflow ÷ volume = 180 ÷ 33.6 = 5.4 ACH.

questions.questionText: Outside air is clearly lower in g/kg than inside air. What does ventilation do?
options: It removes water from the building
It adds water to the building
It has no effect on moisture
It raises the indoor dew point
questions.explanation: Swapping wetter inside air for drier outside air, in g/kg, carries water out of the building.

questions.questionText: In which NCC climate zones must external walls have a drained and ventilated cavity?
options: Climate zones 1 to 3
Only in climate zone 2
Climate zones 6 to 8
Climate zones 4 and 5
questions.explanation: The ABCB handbook summarises that in climate zones 6 to 8 external walls must incorporate a drained and ventilated cavity.

questions.questionText: A NZ rental living room must be able to be heated to at least what?
questions.explanation: The Healthy Homes Standards set the required heating capacity to heat the living room to at least 18 °C.

questions.questionText: What does the ABCB condensation method compare for outdoor overnight condensation?
options: Mean minimum temperature with dew point
Mean rainfall with mean wind speed
Mean maximum temperature with cloud cover
Mean sunshine hours with mean RH
questions.explanation: Where the monthly mean minimum falls below the mean dew point, condensation may occur under suitable surface and exposure conditions.

questions.questionText: What is grain depression across a dehumidifier?
options: Inlet g/kg minus outlet g/kg
Outlet RH minus inlet RH
Outlet °C minus inlet °C
Tank litres minus pump litres
questions.explanation: Grain depression is the inlet humidity ratio minus the outlet humidity ratio, reported in g/kg.

questions.questionText: Two units draw 1000 W each at 230 V. What current do they draw together?
options: About 4.3 A
About 8.7 A
About 10.9 A
About 17.4 A
questions.explanation: I = P ÷ V = 2000 ÷ 230 = 8.7 A, which leaves little headroom on a 10 A circuit.
